moonwell_blighted_roots.description:
Grove Warden Pennarin. Come to the rail and look down at the water before we talk.

The Moonwell's roots are coming up black at the edges.

Not the whole root. The edges - which is the part that's kept me awake, because a thing that dies all at once has been killed and a thing that goes black at the edges is being fed something.

I need samples, and I need them off the Rootbinders rather than out of the ground.

That's deliberate. Anything I pull up myself has already been in that soil and I can't tell you what it picked up on the way. What they carry is what they're putting IN.

They sing to the roots. I've stood close enough to hear it.

And the roots sing back, which is ordinary and lovely and the reason I took this post.

The song is wrong. Bring me what they're carrying, before this reaches the Grove proper.
moonwell_blighted_roots.accept_text: Off the Twilight Rootbinders, below the Moonwell.
moonwell_blighted_roots.turn_in_text:
Black at the core. And warm.

That is not sap.

Thank you. Now at least we know how deep it goes, which is worse than not knowing and better than guessing.

moonwell_gloomcap_sacs.description:
Sentinel Liaison Valea. I'll keep this short - you've a long way down.

There's a question the healers can't answer from up here and it decides everything we do next.

Can the spread be burned out, or must it be cut out?

Those are not similar answers. Burning is three nights and some unhappy druids. Cutting is a season, a cordon, and telling Astranaar that its Moonwell is closed.

I'd very much like to know which before I write to anybody.

So: spore sacs, off the sporelings below the Moonwell.

Gently. They burst, and if one goes you will smell it for a week and so will everyone standing near you.

Unbroken. That's not fastidiousness - a burst sac tells the healers nothing except that it burst.
moonwell_gloomcap_sacs.accept_text: Off the sporelings below the Moonwell. Unbroken.
moonwell_gloomcap_sacs.turn_in_text:
Unbroken. Every one.

I'm impressed, and I'd expected to be writing a different note this evening.

The healers will want to know what these have been feeding on.

moonwell_hollow_cull.description:
The things beneath the Moonwell are growing bolder, and I can date it to the week.

Rotlashers and corrupted Moon Guards, crowding the way down, and the Rootbinders working behind them.

I sent a party in eleven days ago.

They were braver than they were wise and I let them go, because they were certain and I was tired, and I've had eleven days to think about which of those did the deciding.

Thin the Hollow so the next party can reach the grove at the bottom.

That's the whole object. Not clear it - reach it. Nobody has stood in that grove since this started and every judgement we've made has been from the stair.

Go down in company.

The Hollow was never meant to be walked alone, even before. It is not what it was.
moonwell_hollow_cull.accept_text: Down into the Hollow, below the Moonwell.
moonwell_hollow_cull.turn_in_text:
You came back.

That is more than the last party managed.

Sit. Eat something. I'll want the rest of it in a moment and not before.

moonwell_mosshide.description:
There's an old gloomcap at the heart of the spread, the size of a house, and the Sentinels call it Mosshide.

Here's the thing I need you to hold on to before you go down.

Mosshide isn't the corruption. It was there before - longer than the Moonwell's lamps, longer than the Sentinels, and I've found it on a chart drawn before anyone in Astranaar was born.

It's the anchor.

Whatever came into this Hollow needed something already rooted and already old to hang itself on, and it found the oldest thing down there and used it.

Cut it down and the rot loses its hold.

I've argued with myself about this for a fortnight and I've lost every round of it.

It will not go quietly. It has no reason to and nothing was ever asked of it.
moonwell_mosshide.accept_text: At the heart of the Hollow's spread.
moonwell_mosshide.turn_in_text:
Then the spread has a hole in it. Good.

Rest. Properly rest - Maelwyn is next, and she will be harder for reasons that have nothing to do with the fight.

moonwell_maelwyn.description:
[Pennarin takes a long time to start.]

Maelwyn Blightbloom was a Moonwell keeper.

She held this post before me. She taught me the lamps, and how to read the water's colour at dusk, and most of what I've been using to work out what's wrong down there came from her.

Now she is the Blight's flower. That's the Sentinels' phrase and I've not been able to improve on it.

She's at the Moonwell itself, at the bottom of the Hollow, and as long as she stands in that water it will not run clean.

End her there.

She still has the face I remember. I want you to have been told that rather than discover it - people have gone down not knowing and come back up unable to say why they hesitated.

Don't let it slow your hand.

Do it for her. I've thought about that phrasing a long while and I mean it exactly.
moonwell_maelwyn.accept_text: At the Moonwell, at the bottom of the Hollow.
moonwell_maelwyn.turn_in_text:
...Thank you.

I'll tell the others the water is clear.

I will not tell them how it looked, and I'd ask the same of you.

barrows_hunters_horns.description:
Grunt Bloodfang. You'll be the one Vashj keeps talking about. Fine. Here's a job.

The huntsmen buried in the Barrows carry their horns.

Still. In the ground, after however long it's been - and nobody at this post can tell me how long, which I've stopped finding odd and started finding useful.

I want them gone, and I'll be honest that my reason isn't complicated.

Those horns call the dead out of the hill. That's not a story the night elves tell, that's a thing I've stood on this wall and heard happen, twice, both times an hour before something came down the road at us.

Stop the calling and I'm happy.

And some of that horn-bone might ring true for a Horde signal. I'd not lead with that, but I'm not going to pretend it hasn't occurred to me.

I don't care whose horns they were. Neither will you, once you've heard one.
barrows_hunters_horns.accept_text: Off the huntsmen in the Barrows.
barrows_hunters_horns.turn_in_text:
Hm.

It still howls when the wind touches it. Gives me the chills and I don't get those.

Good work.

barrows_rimebone_cull.description:
Interrogator Vashj. I want the Barrows quiet, and I'd like to tell you precisely what I mean by quiet because it isn't a figure of speech.

That hill sings.

Not loudly. You have to be on the north wall at the right hour, and once you've heard it you hear it every night after, which is its own problem and not one I'll trouble you with.

It's the Hunt's old song. And it keeps being sung because the Hunt-King's road is still being kept.

The rimebone hounds keep it. The wights keep it. They walk a route that has not changed in however many centuries and the walking is what holds the song together.

Break the route and the song has nothing carrying it.

Dead things in a cold hole. It is not complicated.

Go in with friends, come out with the job done.
barrows_rimebone_cull.accept_text: In the Barrows, along the Hunt-King's road.
barrows_rimebone_cull.turn_in_text:
The howling's thinner.

Not gone. Not yet.

That's your next job and I'd rather you heard that now than at the end of a drink.

barrows_wintermaw.description:
There's a hound chained in the Houndkeepers' Crypt the size of a warhorse.

Chained. That's the part worth sitting with - somebody put it there on purpose, and somebody wanted it to stay, and whoever that was has been dust for a very long time.

The chains are old.

The grudge is older, and I don't use that word loosely. I've interrogated a lot of things and I can tell the difference between a beast that's angry and a beast that's been waiting.

It will not come to you.

That's the whole tactical content of what I've got. Everything else in that hill ranges - the hounds run the road, the wights walk it. This one stays where it was put and makes you come into the room.

So you will go to it.

Take a healer. And take a good reason, because you'll want one about halfway down the stair.
barrows_wintermaw.accept_text: The Houndkeepers' Crypt, in the Barrows.
barrows_wintermaw.turn_in_text:
That howl has stopped.

I did not know how much of the wind it had been until it stopped, and now the wind sounds wrong to me, which I suppose is fair.

barrows_hunt_king.description:
War Mage Grimtotem. Sit if you like, I've been standing at this map since the hounds went quiet.

At the end of the Barrows lies Hunt-King Valorin.

Still hunting. In his sleep, which is a sentence I've written in three reports now and had queried every time.

Here's what it means in practice, and it's why I won't leave it alone.

The Wild Hunt never ended. It went underground - the whole apparatus of it, the king, the road, the hounds, the horns - and it has been running down there uninterrupted for as long as that hill has stood.

And a hunt ranges. That's what a hunt is. It does not stay within a boundary because the boundary is new and the hunt is not.

I will not have a dead king's hunt ranging over Horde land because nobody wanted to go into the hill.

Let's make sure it stays underground.
barrows_hunt_king.accept_text: At the deepest end of the Barrows.
barrows_hunt_king.turn_in_text:
He rode out of the world a long time ago.

Now he's finally ridden all the way home.

I'll take the map down.

groms_garrison_cull.description:
Grom's Rest has become a demon barracks and I want you to take that word literally.

Not an infestation. A barracks.

Satyrs, imps and fel-touched hounds crowding the hall beyond the gate - and they're billeted. There's an order to where they sleep. I've had eyes on that gate for three weeks and the same ones come out at the same hours.

Things that crawl out of a tear in the world don't keep a roster.

So somebody is running it, and whatever he's running it for is behind that hall rather than in it.

Thin the garrison so a real party can push through to find out.

And I'll say this once: this is a dungeon, not a stroll. Bring a full party and bring your potions.

Then bring me proof the hall is clearer, because I am not going to tell Splintertree a thing I have not been handed.
groms_garrison_cull.accept_text: The hall beyond the gate at Grom's Rest.
groms_garrison_cull.turn_in_text:
Good. The gate is no longer a wall of bodies.

Now find out what they're guarding, because I promise you it isn't the hall.

groms_legion_brands.description:
Something I want off the Felguard Legionnaires, and it isn't a trophy.

They wear a fel-iron plate stamped with the Legion's mark.

Stamped. In a foundry, by a process, with a die that somebody cut - which means there is a supply line, and a supply line has a beginning and the beginning is somewhere a person could walk to.

That's what I actually do here. Everyone assumes an interrogator works on prisoners. Most of what I've ever learned, I've learned off equipment.

So bring me a handful and I'll trace where the Legion's gold is coming from.

Take them off the dead, not the living.

I'm aware that reads as a joke. It is not - a legionnaire will let you get a hand on that plate, and the three seconds it takes to work it loose are the three seconds he's waiting for.
groms_legion_brands.accept_text: Off the felguard legionnaires inside Grom's Rest.
groms_legion_brands.turn_in_text:
These are stamped in a Legion foundry I know. I know the die, I know the hand that cut it.

Someone is shipping weapons through Ashenvale.

And I know exactly who to ask about it, which I did not this morning.

groms_satyr_warlord.description:
The Satyr Warlord rules the western hall.

I'll be straight with you, because you'd work it out anyway and resent me for it: he's a detour. The road to the throne doesn't go through him and nothing behind him matters.

Skippable. I know.

Do it anyway, and here's the argument.

A warlord left alive is a warlord that recruits. That's not a maxim, that's what I've watched happen in this forest twice - we push through, we take the throne, we declare it finished, and eighteen months later the hall has a new garrison in it built around the one loud thing nobody bothered to kill.

His head sends a message to the satyrs who'd be doing the rebuilding.

That's worth a detour. I've stopped apologising for asking.
groms_satyr_warlord.accept_text: The western hall of Grom's Rest.
groms_satyr_warlord.turn_in_text:
Good.

That kind of loud ends in a very particular silence, and the ones who were listening to him will have heard it.

groms_void_handmaiden.description:
Eastern gathering. There's a Void Handmaiden in it and she's binding satyrs to something that was not made to be bound.

I want to be careful about how I explain this, because people hear 'demon dungeon' and bring the wrong preparation.

Void magic is not like fel.

Fel burns. It's hostile and loud and it tells you what it's doing to you while it does it, and every fel ward we own was built around that.

Void forgets.

It doesn't hurt you in a way you'll notice. It takes things out of the room - a name, a direction, the fact that somebody was standing to your left - and it does it so quietly that the party doesn't realise it's down a member until the fight is over.

So take someone who remembers you.

That's the actual instruction. Not a healer. Someone who will notice if you stop being there.
groms_void_handmaiden.accept_text: The eastern gathering hall of Grom's Rest.
groms_void_handmaiden.turn_in_text:
I feel lighter.

I think it is lighter. I've been standing in the same tent for a month and something has changed in it and I cannot tell you what.

Thank you.

groms_doomguard.description:
The only road to the throne runs north from the hub, and there's a Doomguard Sentinel standing in it.

It has never once left its post.

I've had that confirmed three separate ways and I keep coming back to it, because everything else in that place moves. The satyrs patrol. The hounds range. The imps go where imps go.

This thing stands in a corridor.

It does not tire. It does not sleep. It does not move - not to pursue, not to flank, not when the hall behind it was being cleared by you a week ago, and that is the detail that tells you what it's actually for.

It isn't guarding the road. It's a door, and somebody shut it.

So you'll have to persuade it. Forcefully, and with everything, because a thing that has stood in one place for years has nothing to spend its strength on but you.
groms_doomguard.accept_text: The north road out of the hub, inside Grom's Rest.
groms_doomguard.turn_in_text:
One down.

Three rooms behind it, and the throne beyond that.

Press on while the road's open - a door like that may not be the only one they had.

groms_corrupted_ancient.description:
Deeper in there's an Ancient, and it has been bent into a demon's horror.

It was a grove warden. That is not me being sentimental about a tree - it had a post, and a stretch of forest, and it did the same work Pennarin does at the Moonwell for longer than the night elves have had a word for the job.

Now it's a thing that rots, and it rots outward, and everything in that chamber is what it's done to the room around it.

Remember it was a protector when your hand slows.

It will slow. I've watched it happen to people considerably harder than either of us, and the ones who weren't told beforehand are the ones it killed.

And then remember that it cannot be saved.

Both of those, in that order. I've not found a way to give you one without the other.
groms_corrupted_ancient.accept_text: In the deep chambers of Grom's Rest.
groms_corrupted_ancient.turn_in_text:
I'll tell the druids it fell fighting.

That is as close to the truth as they can bear, and closer than I'd manage if they asked twice.

groms_felguard_overseer.description:
The Bone Hall. Last gate before the Inner Sanctum, and a Felguard Overseer holds it.

Here's why he's mine rather than Grimtotem's.

An overseer answers to somebody. That's the entire function - he isn't there to fight, he's there so that whatever's in the Sanctum doesn't have to speak to a garrison.

And a thing that answers to somebody wears proof of it.

Bring me his collar.

If the Legion has a hand in Ashenvale, its fingerprints are on that collar - the make of it, the marks on the inside, who had the authority to put it on him.

I've been building this case off stamped plate and shipping routes for a year.

A collar finishes it. That's one object between me and being able to name the hand, and I have waited a long time to be this close to the end of a sentence.
groms_felguard_overseer.accept_text: The Bone Hall, last gate before the Inner Sanctum.
groms_felguard_overseer.turn_in_text:
A Legion collar. As I thought, and I'd half hoped not.

Now we know who's been sending the demons.

And they don't know we know, which is worth more than everything else you've brought me.

groms_lord_nightmare.description:
At the heart of Grom's Rest, the throne.

And the thing on it is what all of this has been feeding.

That's the shape of the whole place, and it took me the full year to see it. The satyrs, the imps, the hounds, the bindings in the eastern hall - none of that was a garrison defending a position. It was a household keeping something alive.

An eldritch horror. I'll use the words even though they're imprecise, because the precise ones would take an hour and you're going anyway.

Kill it and the throne is empty, and Ashenvale stops paying for it.

I have no better advice than this, and I've thought hard about whether to give it at all.

Don't look at it directly.

And don't die, which I'm aware is not advice. I've nothing else and I'd rather say so than invent something.
groms_lord_nightmare.accept_text: The throne at the heart of Grom's Rest.
groms_lord_nightmare.turn_in_text:
...The silence is unbelievable.

I've had a map on this table for a year and I don't know what to do with the table.

Rest, hero. You earned the quiet, and so did this forest.

bfd_garrison.description:
Lookout Taelanor. Up here, where I can keep one eye on the water while we talk.

There's a flooded temple under the cliffs and the naga have been going in and out of it for weeks.

It's a garrison. Not a raid.

That distinction is the whole of my report and nobody above me has wanted to read it. A raid comes, takes, and goes. A garrison arrives and stays and gets reinforced, and you only know which you're looking at by counting.

So I've been counting.

I've counted them going in.

I have not counted them coming out.

That's the part that frightens me, and I've had three weeks to find a better explanation and I haven't got one.

Thin the warriors before it empties onto the Strand.

Go down in company. Whatever's holding that many naga in one hole is not going to be a pleasant surprise.
bfd_garrison.accept_text: The flooded temple under the Zoram cliffs.
bfd_garrison.turn_in_text:
They'll replace them. Not tonight, though.

I wrote the number down. I'm glad it isn't higher, and I'm aware that's a strange thing to be glad about.

bfd_ghamoo_ra.description:
There's a turtle in the outer caverns the naga revere as a god.

I'd find that almost sweet if it weren't the size of a boat and hungry.

And I want to be careful here, because I've watched people treat 'they worship it' as a reason to be gentle, and it is not a reason to be anything.

Ghamoo-ra is a beast. The worship is theirs, not its. It has no idea it's a god and it will not fight like one - it'll fight like something very large that has never had to learn.

What it does is block the way inward.

That's its actual role, whatever they say at the altar. Nothing gets deeper into those caverns past it, and that includes us, and that is why it has been left alive and fed.

Break it, and take the way.

I'd not ask if there were another road. I've looked for one for three weeks.
bfd_ghamoo_ra.accept_text: The outer caverns of the drowned temple.
bfd_ghamoo_ra.turn_in_text:
A god, they said.

It died as easily as a turtle.

I'll remember that the next time I hear the naga pray, and I hear them most nights.

bfd_lady_sarevess.description:
Lady Sarevess commands the naga of the upper halls, and she's the reason the garrison works.

I've spent three weeks establishing that rather than assuming it, and here's the evidence.

They don't fight each other. Naga do. Every naga band I've ever watched on this coast has spent half its strength on internal argument, and this one doesn't, and that doesn't happen without somebody holding the chair hard.

If she falls, they'll fight over the chair for a month.

That's a month the Strand sleeps. I'm not promising you more than that and I won't pretend it's a victory.

She will offer you terms.

I'd not read them. I know how that sounds and I know you'll want to, and I'm telling you anyway because the last Sentinel who read them is still in Astranaar and still not right.

Cut her down and spare me the sound of her voice in my dreams.
bfd_lady_sarevess.accept_text: The upper halls of the drowned temple.
bfd_lady_sarevess.turn_in_text:
Without her they'll fight over that chair for a month.

That's a month the Strand sleeps.

Thank you. I'll take the sleep and not ask what it cost.

bfd_gelihast.description:
Right - you're the one who's been going down there. Good, because nobody else will listen to this.

Illyen. I build boats, which in Zoram'gar means I mostly rebuild boats.

Gelihast has gathered the Deeps' murlocs under one banner. That's the official half of it and the Lookout will tell you it matters, and she's right, and I don't care.

He wears my net as a crown.

MY net. Off my boat. The one I lost in spring, that I knotted myself, that took a week and cost me a thumbnail.

And he wears it. On his head. Deliberately.

Bring it back.

It's patched, it stinks, and it is worth nothing to any person alive including me.

I want it.

And scatter the rest of them while you're in there, since you'll be down that way regardless.
bfd_gelihast.accept_text: Among the murlocs in the Deeps. He's wearing the net.
bfd_gelihast.turn_in_text:
That's my knot! Look at that - he left the knot in.

The fool.

Thank you. I'll sink another boat in his honour, which at my rate will be a fortnight.

bfd_hydra_fangs.description:
Second thing, and this one's actually professional.

The murloc hydras down in the Deeps shed their fangs.

And a hydra fang will cut a rope under tension and never go dull. I want to be precise about that because every boatwright on this coast has heard the claim and about half of them think it's a story.

It is not a story. I've had one for two years. I have cut standing rigging with it, under load, at sea, and it is exactly as sharp now as the day I took it off the thing.

I don't know why. I've asked a druid and I've asked a goblin and got two confident answers that disagreed.

Bring me a handful for the rack.

And then I'll have a tool rack worth showing off, and I'll sharpen nothing for a year, and that is the whole of my ambition this season.
bfd_hydra_fangs.accept_text: Off the hydras in the Deeps. They shed them.
bfd_hydra_fangs.turn_in_text:
And not a chip on them. Not one.

These are going straight in the rack.

I'll sharpen nothing for a year and I'll be insufferable about it.

bfd_tide_callers.description:
Two of the deeper masters hold the inner temple, and they are not a pair.

Lorgus Jett commands the tide.

Old Serra'kis commands what the tide has swallowed - and I want you to notice that those are different offices, because it took me a long while to understand that the temple has two of them on purpose.

One brings the water in. The other keeps whatever comes with it.

That's not a garrison arrangement. That's a temple's, and it's been running that way since long before the naga we're fighting were born.

You'll have to go through both. There's no route that takes one and leaves the other.

It is not a job for fewer than a full party. Lookout or not, I'd not go down there with less and I've been watching that water for three weeks.
bfd_tide_callers.accept_text: The inner temple of the Deeps - both of them.
bfd_tide_callers.turn_in_text:
Both.

I felt the water settle. Actually felt it, from up here on the wall.

I'd have missed it entirely if I'd been looking at the sea instead of at you.

bfd_kelris.description:
Twilight Lord Kelris is at the temple's heart, and he is the reason any of this is happening.

The naga were here first. The murlocs have always been here. Neither of them built this.

He puts the Twilight's Hammer's work in the mouths of dying men.

That's not a flourish and I'd like you to have it plainly. I've pulled three people off this shore in three weeks who should have been past speaking and were not, and all three said the same thing, and none of them had ever met each other.

I wrote it down the first time. I didn't the second.

I want him silent.

He works in whispers - that's the whole of his method and it's why nobody's stopped him.

Do not listen. Cut him down.
bfd_kelris.accept_text: The heart of the drowned temple.
bfd_kelris.turn_in_text:
Silent.

I'd forgotten silence could be so loud.

One more below him, and then it ends.

bfd_aku_mai.description:
At the bottom of Blackfathom, under all of it, Aku'mai sleeps.

The naga call it the Devourer. They don't call it a god - I want that noted, because they call the turtle a god and they do not call this one anything so small.

Everything you've done down there has been about this.

The garrison. The tide-callers. Kelris in the heart whispering into dying men. None of that was a war on the Strand. It was an apparatus around a sleeping thing, and whether they were keeping it asleep or getting it ready I have never been able to decide.

If it wakes, the Strand is the least of the world's worries.

It's the last thing in the Deeps.

Kill it while it sleeps, or don't go at all. I mean that as given - there's no third version of this where somebody has a look first.

I'll be on the wall. I will be watching the water.
bfd_aku_mai.accept_text: The lowest chamber of Blackfathom Deeps.
bfd_aku_mai.turn_in_text:
Then it's over.

I'll sleep tonight. Three weeks on that wall and I'll sleep tonight.

You earned that, and the Strand's gratitude. Take the pearl, if it still glows.
